title: Alquilando una casa
desc: Your own place, and a contract you half understand

sn.s: Después de un año quiero mi propia casa.
sn.e: After a year I want my own place.

sn.s: Doña Carmen no se pone contenta.
sn.e: Doña Carmen is not happy about it.

sn.s: Pero entiende.
sn.e: But she understands.

sn.s: "Está bien, mijo. Pero cerca", dice ella.
sn.e: "That's all right, mijo. But close by," she says.

sn.s: Don Beto conoce a un señor que alquila.
sn.e: Don Beto knows a man who rents places out.

sn.s: El señor tiene una casa a tres cuadras.
sn.e: The man has a house three blocks away.

sn.s: Vamos a verla un sábado.
sn.e: We go to see it on a Saturday.

sn.s: La casa es chiquita.
sn.e: The house is small.

sn.s: Tiene dos cuartos y una cocina.
sn.e: It has two rooms and a kitchen.

sn.s: Tiene un patio atrás con una pila.
sn.e: It has a patio at the back with a pila.

sn.s: El techo es de zinc.
sn.e: The roof is corrugated iron.

sn.s: Con lluvia va a hacer un ruido tremendo.
sn.e: In the rain it is going to make a tremendous noise.

sn.s: "¿Cuánto es el alquiler?", pregunto yo.
sn.e: "How much is the rent?" I ask.

sn.s: "Cuatro mil al mes", dice el dueño.
sn.e: "Four thousand a month," the owner says.

sn.s: Don Beto hace una cara.
sn.e: Don Beto pulls a face.

sn.s: "Está caro para este barrio", dice él.
sn.e: "That's dear for this barrio," he says.

sn.s: El dueño y don Beto hablan un rato.
sn.e: The owner and don Beto talk for a while.

sn.s: Yo no digo nada, porque no me toca.
sn.e: I say nothing, because it is not my place.

sn.s: Al final acuerdan tres mil quinientos.
sn.e: In the end they agree on three and a half thousand.

sn.s: Después viene lo del depósito.
sn.e: Then comes the deposit.

sn.s: El dueño quiere dos meses de depósito.
sn.e: The owner wants two months as a deposit.

sn.s: Don Beto dice que uno.
sn.e: Don Beto says one.

sn.s: Acuerdan uno y medio.
sn.e: They agree on one and a half.

sn.s: "¿Y el contrato?", pregunto yo.
sn.e: "And the contract?" I ask.

sn.s: El dueño me mira sin entender.
sn.e: The owner looks at me without understanding.

sn.s: "¿Cuál contrato?", dice él.
sn.e: "What contract?" he says.

sn.s: No hay papel y no hay que firmar nada.
sn.e: There is no paper and nothing to sign.

sn.s: El acuerdo es lo que dijimos aquí.
sn.e: The agreement is what we said here.

sn.s: Con don Beto de testigo.
sn.e: With don Beto as witness.

sn.s: Eso me pone nervioso.
sn.e: That makes me nervous.

sn.s: Yo quiero algo escrito.
sn.e: I want something in writing.

sn.s: Don Beto me habla afuera.
sn.e: Don Beto talks to me outside.

sn.s: "Si pide papel, él va a pensar mal."
sn.e: "If you ask for paper, he's going to think badly of you."

sn.s: "Va a pensar que usted no confía."
sn.e: "He'll think you don't trust him."

sn.s: "¿Y si después dice otra cosa?", pregunto.
sn.e: "And if he says something different later?" I ask.

sn.s: "Yo estuve aquí", dice don Beto.
sn.e: "I was here," don Beto says.

sn.s: Y eso, aquí, es el contrato.
sn.e: And that, here, is the contract.

sn.s: Le pago el depósito y me da las llaves.
sn.e: I pay him the deposit and he gives me the keys.

sn.s: Son dos llaves en un alambre.
sn.e: It is two keys on a piece of wire.

sn.s: Me mudo el domingo.
sn.e: I move in on the Sunday.

sn.s: Roberto y dos primos me ayudan.
sn.e: Roberto and two cousins help me.

sn.s: No tengo casi nada que mudar.
sn.e: I have almost nothing to move.

sn.s: Una maleta, unos libros, un abanico.
sn.e: A suitcase, some books, a fan.

sn.s: Doña Carmen me manda una olla y dos platos.
sn.e: Doña Carmen sends me a pot and two plates.

sn.s: Me manda una silla y un balde.
sn.e: She sends me a chair and a bucket.

sn.s: Y me manda comida hecha para tres días.
sn.e: And she sends me food cooked for three days.

sn.s: La primera noche la casa suena rara.
sn.e: The first night the house sounds strange.

sn.s: Es la primera vez que duermo solo aquí.
sn.e: It is the first time I sleep alone here.

sn.s: Al otro día doña Carmen llega a las siete.
sn.e: The next day doña Carmen arrives at seven.

sn.s: Llega con gallo pinto y con café.
sn.e: She arrives with gallo pinto and coffee.

sn.s: "Es que le queda cerca", dice ella.
sn.e: "It's just that it's close by," she says.

sn.s: Y son tres cuadras.
sn.e: And it is three blocks.
